# 2 Kings Chapter 19 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 240v–241v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_019_page_479.jpg, 2KI_019_page_480.jpg, 2KI_019_page_481.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.

**2** He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

**3** They said to him, "Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of distress, of rebuke, and of disgrace. Children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.

**4** It may be that the LORD your God has heard all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria sent to mock the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that is left."

**5** When the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah,

**6** Isaiah said to them, "Say to your master: Thus says the LORD: Do not be afraid because of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.

**7** Behold, I will put a spirit in him, so that he shall hear a rumor and return to his own land, and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land."

**8** The Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.

**9** Now the king heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, "He has set out to fight against you." So he again sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

**10** "Thus shall you speak to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by promising that Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.

**11** Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, devoting them to destruction. And shall you be delivered?

**12** Have the gods of the nations delivered them — the nations that my fathers destroyed: Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?

**13** Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, the king of Hena, or the king of Ivvah?"

**14** Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread it before the LORD.

**15** And Hezekiah prayed before the LORD: "O LORD, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you are the God — you alone — of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.

**16** Incline your ear, O LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, O LORD, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to mock the living God.

**17** Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands

**18** and have cast their gods into the fire, for they were not gods but the work of human hands — wood and stone — and so they were destroyed.

**19** Now, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, O LORD, are God alone."

**20** Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I have heard your prayer to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria."

**21** This is the word that the LORD has spoken concerning him:

She despises you, she mocks you —
    the virgin daughter of Zion.
She shakes her head behind you —
    the daughter of Jerusalem.

**22** Whom have you mocked and blasphemed?
    Against whom have you raised your voice
    and lifted your eyes on high?
    Against the Holy One of Israel!

**23** By your messengers you have mocked the Lord and said,
    'With my many chariots I have gone up
    the heights of the mountains,
    to the far recesses of Lebanon.
I cut down its tallest cedars,
    its choicest cypresses.
I entered its farthest lodge,
    its densest forest.

**24** I dug wells and drank foreign waters,
    and with the sole of my foot I dried up
    all the streams of Egypt.'

**25** Have you not heard?
    Long ago I planned it;
    in ancient times I formed it.
Now I have brought it to pass,
    that fortified cities should become
    ruined heaps of stone.

**26** Their inhabitants, powerless,
    were dismayed and put to shame.
They became like plants of the field
    and tender green shoots,
like grass on the rooftops,
    scorched before it can grow.

**27** I know your sitting down,
    your going out and coming in,
    and your raging against me.

**28** Because you have raged against me
    and your arrogance has reached my ears,
I will put my hook in your nose
    and my bit in your lips,
and I will turn you back
    by the way that you came.

**29** "And this shall be the sign for you: this year eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that. But in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

**30** The surviving remnant of the house of Judah shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.

**31** For out of Jerusalem shall go a remnant, and out of Mount Zion a band of survivors. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this.

**32** "Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria: He shall not come into this city or shoot an arrow there, or come before it with a shield, or cast up a siege ramp against it.

**33** By the way that he came, by the same he shall return, and he shall not come into this city, declares the LORD.

**34** For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David."

**35** That very night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down one hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians. When they arose in the morning, behold, they were all dead bodies.

**36** Then Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went home, and lived in Nineveh.

**37** And as he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, struck him down with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter completes the pattern begun in chapter 18: crisis (Rabshakeh's speech) leads to prayer (Hezekiah in the temple) leads to prophetic oracle (Isaiah's word) leads to deliverance (the angel's strike). It is the definitive "prayer and deliverance" narrative of the Hebrew Bible. Hezekiah's prayer (vv.15-19) is a masterpiece of theological argument: he begins with YHWH's identity as the one true God, acknowledges the reality of Assyria's power, then distinguishes YHWH from the conquered gods — those were "wood and stone," but YHWH is the living God. Isaiah's oracle (vv.21-28) is the theological counterpoint to Sennacherib's boasts: where Sennacherib claimed his own power, YHWH reveals that Assyria's conquests were divine instruments, not human achievements. The "hook in your nose" imagery (v.28) reverses the Assyrians' own practice of leading captives by nose-rings. The overnight destruction (v.35) is narrated with deliberate understatement — the greatest military catastrophe in the ancient world, told in a single verse. Sennacherib's death in his own god's temple (v.37) completes the irony: the king who mocked the living God is murdered in the house of a dead one.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.3 — "birth-opening" vs. "point of birth" vs. "woman in labor"
- **EMET:** "the-children have-come to-the-birth-opening [mashber]"
- **LOGOS:** "Children have come to the point of birth"
- **PNEUMA:** "We are like a woman in labor who has no strength left to deliver her child"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them" — LOGOS preserves the metaphor without over-expanding it. PNEUMA's rendering explains too much; EMET's "birth-opening" is too clinical.

### V.6 — "servants" vs. "underlings"
- **EMET:** "the-servants [na'arey] of-the-king of-Ashur"
- **LOGOS:** "the servants of the king of Assyria"
- **PNEUMA:** "the king of Assyria's underlings"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the servants of the king of Assyria" — *na'ar* can mean servant or young man. "Servants" is neutral; "underlings" (PNEUMA) imports a dismissive tone not clearly in YHWH's speech.

### V.21 — Poetry formatting
- **EMET:** Prose format with bracketed Hebrew
- **LOGOS:** Indented poetry with line breaks
- **PNEUMA:** Indented poetry with line breaks
- **SOPHIA ruling:** Indented poetry — vv.21-28 are clearly poetic oracle and should be formatted as verse, following LOGOS/PNEUMA.

### V.28 — "bit in your lips" vs. "bit in your mouth"
- **EMET:** "my-bit [u-mitiggi] in-your-lips [be-sefateykha]"
- **LOGOS:** "my bit in your lips"
- **PNEUMA:** "my bit in your mouth"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "my bit in your lips" — the Hebrew specifies *sefatayim* (lips), not *peh* (mouth). LOGOS follows the Hebrew precisely.

### V.31 — "zeal" vs. "passionate commitment"
- **EMET:** "the-zeal [qin'at] of-YHWH"
- **LOGOS:** "The zeal of the LORD of hosts"
- **PNEUMA:** "The passionate commitment of the LORD of Armies"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "The zeal of the LORD of hosts" — *qin'ah* is traditionally rendered "zeal" in this formulaic phrase (cf. Isa 9:7). "Passionate commitment" is accurate but loses the traditional resonance. *Tseva'ot* = "hosts" (not "Armies").

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
